content.title: Back on top: UConn wins its 12th national championship
content.text: TAMPA, FL (WFSB) - Sunday marked the final day of the women’s college basketball season.The University of Connecticut women’s basketball team eyed its 12th national title.In its way was the University of South Carolina.The two teams were on a collision course in Tampa, FL.However, UConn ran right through the Gamecocks. The final was 82-59.How it played outSouth Carolina drew first blood with a three.UConn freshman Sarah Strong answered with a bank shot.The Gamecocks were physical to open the game. They led early, 11-10, with 5:40 to go in the first quarter.Then Azzi Fudd got an and-one to put UConn on top 13-11.Azzi Fudd (35) shoots against South Carolina forward Sania Feagin (20) during the first half of the national championship at the Final Four of the women's college basketball tournament, Sunday, April 6, 2025, in Tampa, Fla.(AP Photo / Chris O'Meara)At the first media timeout, UConn led 15-13.By the end of the quarter, UConn’s lead grew, 19-14. Fudd led all scorers with 7 points.The Huskies opened the second quarter with back-to-back Paige Bueckers and Strong buckets. That put their led at 9 with 9 min. to go until halftime.The Gamecocks stormed back to get the game within 5.UConn struggled from beyond the arc, and that allowed South Carolina to claw back to within 3. The team was 0-6 with about 5:00 to go in the quarter.However, Bueckers put the lead back at 7, 29-22, with 3:50 left.A Fudd steal and fastbreak put the Huskies up 11 with about 3:00 to go.UConn took a 36-26 lead into the locker room at the half, thanks to a 3 from Ashlynn Shade.Fudd continued to lead in the scoring column with 13.UConn’s Jana El Alfy picked up a fourth foul at the 6:27 mark of the third and had to be subbed out. UConn still led 40-29 at that point.Fudd, meanwhile, continued to dominate. She put the Huskies up by 15 with about 5:30 to go. She was up to 21.A pair of threes from Fudd and Strong put the Huskies up 56-40.At the end of the third, the lead was 20. Fudd and Bueckers played the entire game up until that point.In the fourth, UConn’s defense led to offense and helped put the lead at 26, 70-44, with 8:20 to to go in the game.Bueckers heard MVP chants from the crowd. She was up to 17 points as the UConn lead grew to 29 with 7:19 to go.A Strong three put UConn in front by 30 with 5:30 left.The Huskies cruised from that point.Strong scored her 114th point in the entire NCAA Tournament, the most by a freshman in Division I history.Bueckers and Fudd finally came out at the 1:32 mark. Bueckers immediately embraced coach Geno Auriemma.Strong and Fudd led the team with 24 points each. Strong also was a menace on the boards, snaring 15 rebounds.Fudd ended up earning the tournament’s most outstanding player award.Legacies were on the lineEvery team’s goal is to be playing on the last possible day.The UConn women's basketball team arrives at the arena ahead of its NCAA Tournament championship matchup against South Carolina on April 6, 2025.(WFSB)Looking at the two teams, UConn with its legacy and South Carolina with its recent legacy, they are arguably the two most prominent teams in women’s college basketball.”UConn, they’re the center of women’s basketball, 11 national championships. Who wouldn’t want to have 11 championships,” said South Carolina’s Te-Hena Paopao.”That’s what we’ve all dreamed of, we came to Connecticut to compete. Being able to accomplish that, to do it with this group of seniors,” said UConn’s Azzi Fudd.There was a lot of talk about Paige Bueckers’ legacy and whether or not she needs to win a national championship to cement hers.“I don’t think that’s up to me,” Bueckers said at Saturday’s UConn media availability. “That’s up to the people who get to decide what legacies are cemented. I’m not worried about it at all”.”For someone who invested as much as she has, given to UConn, the community, her teammates, the love of the game, she deserves to get a national championship,” UConn coach Geno Auriemma said.UConn and South Carolina have met beforeThe two teams played earlier this season. UConn went down to South Carolina and won by 30.Everyone talking about this game said not to put too much emphasis on the last time they played.That game in February was a shocker at the time. The Huskies had lost three games already, but the 87-58 win in Columbia put them right back in the conversation as the team to beat.”I think that was a pivotal game for us,” Fudd said, “but that game [for] tomorrow means nothing. We’re different teams now, a lot of learning, a lot of basketball played in between.””I think that win gave us a lot of confidence,“ said UConn’s Kaitlyn Chen. “One of the first times, it really showed we can play together as a team, but it has nothing to do with [Sunday’s] game. It’s 0-0, a tough matchup.”South Carolina’s Raven Johnson said her team needed to bring its A game.”UConn, they thrive on bad basketball, bad shots,“ Johnson said. ”If we play good basketball, move the ball, we should be good.”Maybe that 30 point win at South Carolina was a fluke, but the fact is, the Huskies haven’t lost a game since.It was one last game for South Carolina, which had won two of the last three titles.UConn, with its 11 titles, had not won one since 2016.Going into the tournament, the season had been full of ups and downs for the Huskies.From early season injuries to heartbreaking regular season losses, the year was far from perfect for UConn.Questions were asked about whether they could hang with the top teams in the tournament and if the Huskies had what it took to become champions.They would go on to win all of their NCAA Tournament games by at least 23 points.With their 12th title victory, they are now the winningest program in Division I college basketball history. They were previously tied with the UCLA men’s program, who won 11 national championships under legendary coach John Wooden.Copyright 2025 WFSB. All rights reserved.
